steps.title: Multiply by conjugate
steps.narration: Multiply numerator and denominator by root three minus root two to rationalise the denominator.

steps.title: Simplify denominator
steps.narration: Difference of squares turns the denominator into three minus two, which equals one.

steps.title: Expand and collect numerator
steps.narration: Expand the top product and combine like surds and whole numbers to get three root six minus seven.

steps.title: Simplified surd
steps.narration: Dividing by one leaves the simplified answer, three root six minus seven.

teach.title: Choose the conjugate
teach.narration: Rewrite the sum in the denominator as root three plus root two so its conjugate root three minus root two gives a positive difference of squares.

teach.title: Multiply top and bottom
teach.narration: Multiply both top and bottom by the conjugate so the value of the fraction stays unchanged.

teach.title: Clear roots in denominator
teach.narration: Using a plus b times a minus b equals a squared minus b squared reduces the denominator to three minus two, or one.

teach.title: Expand numerator brackets
teach.narration: Multiply each term of two root two minus root three by root three minus root two.

teach.title: Collect like terms
teach.narration: Combine two root six plus root six into three root six, and subtract three from minus four to get minus seven.

teach.title: Final expression
teach.narration: Because the denominator is one, the simplified expression is three root six minus seven.

steps.title: Write as powers of 2
steps.narration: Express eight, sixteen, and four as powers of the common base two.

steps.title: Read each logarithm
steps.narration: Because log base two of two to the k equals k, the three logs are three, four, and two.

steps.title: Add and subtract values
steps.narration: Add three and four to get seven, then subtract two.

steps.title: Final value
steps.narration: The value of the expression is five.

teach.title: Evaluate log base 2 of 8
teach.narration: Write eight as two cubed so log base two of eight simplifies directly to three.

teach.title: Evaluate log base 2 of 16
teach.narration: Write sixteen as two to the fourth power, giving log base two of sixteen equal to four.

teach.title: Evaluate log base 2 of 4
teach.narration: Write four as two squared so log base two of four equals two.

teach.title: Substitute and simplify
teach.narration: Substitute the three numbers back in: three plus four minus two equals five.

teach.title: Check with log laws
teach.narration: Check using product and quotient laws: eight times sixteen divided by four is thirty-two, and two to the fifth is thirty-two.

teach.title: Final result
teach.narration: Therefore the expression evaluates to five.

steps.title: Start with equation
steps.narration: We want to isolate g on one side of the equation.

steps.title: Add k and w to both sides
steps.narration: Add k and w to both sides so the term containing g stands alone.

steps.title: Divide both sides by t^{2}
steps.narration: Since t is nonzero, divide both sides by t squared to leave g by itself.

steps.title: Subject of formula
steps.narration: Making g the subject gives k plus w all over t squared.

teach.title: Write the given formula
teach.narration: Identify g inside the first term g t squared, with minus k and minus w subtracted from it.

teach.display: gt^{2} − k − w + k + w = k + w
teach.title: Add k and w to both sides
teach.narration: Add both k and w to each side to cancel the minus k and minus w on the left.

teach.title: Isolate the g term
teach.narration: This leaves g t squared equal to k plus w.

teach.title: Divide both sides by t^{2}
teach.narration: Divide both sides by t squared to undo multiplying g by t squared; this is valid because t is not zero.

teach.title: g in terms of k, w, t
teach.narration: So g equals k plus w divided by t squared.

steps.title: Apply factor theorem
steps.narration: Because y minus one is a factor, substituting y equals one into the polynomial must give zero.

steps.title: Evaluate at y = 1
steps.narration: Replace every y in the polynomial with one and equate to zero.

steps.title: Collect constants
steps.narration: Combine one plus four minus six to get minus one, leaving k minus one equals zero.

steps.title: Value of k
steps.narration: Add one to both sides to get k equals one.

teach.title: State factor theorem
teach.narration: By the factor theorem, y minus one is a factor of f of y only if f of one equals zero.

teach.title: Substitute y = 1
teach.narration: Plug y equals one into each term and set the result equal to zero.

teach.title: Evaluate powers of 1
teach.narration: One cubed is one and four times one squared is four, leaving one plus four plus k minus six equals zero.

teach.title: Add 1 to both sides
teach.narration: Five minus six is minus one; add one to both sides so k stands alone as one.

teach.title: Check with k = 1
teach.narration: Check: substituting k equals one gives one plus four plus one minus six, which is zero.

teach.title: Final value of k
teach.narration: Therefore the value of k is one.

steps.title: Set up variation law
steps.narration: Put direct variable Q in the numerator and inverse variable R in the denominator with constant k.

steps.title: Plug in given values
steps.narration: Substitute P equals twenty-seven, Q equals thirty-six, and R equals sixteen.

steps.title: Find constant k
steps.narration: Multiply both sides by sixteen and divide by thirty-six to obtain k equals twelve.

steps.title: Formula connecting P, Q, R
steps.narration: Replacing k with twelve gives P equals twelve Q over R.

teach.title: Write variation equation
teach.narration: Direct variation puts Q on top, inverse variation puts R underneath, and k is the constant of proportionality.

teach.title: Substitute P, Q, and R
teach.narration: Substitute the known triple twenty-seven, thirty-six, and sixteen into the equation.

teach.title: Isolate constant k
teach.narration: Multiply both sides by sixteen and divide both sides by thirty-six to get k on its own.

teach.title: Cancel common factors
teach.narration: Divide twenty-seven and thirty-six by nine to leave three and four, then divide sixteen by four to get three times four, or twelve.

teach.title: Check with given values
teach.narration: Substitute thirty-six and sixteen back into twelve Q over R to confirm P equals twenty-seven.

teach.title: Final formula
teach.narration: The formula relating the variables is P equals twelve Q over R.

steps.title: Multiply through by 12
steps.narration: Multiply both sides by the common denominator twelve; since twelve is positive, the inequality sign keeps its direction.

steps.title: Clear all fractions
steps.narration: Simplify each fraction to obtain six x plus nine is less than or equal to ten x minus seven.

steps.title: Collect x and constants
steps.narration: Add seven and subtract six x on both sides to get sixteen less than or equal to four x, then divide by four.

steps.title: Solution inequality
steps.narration: Four less than or equal to x reads from x as x greater than or equal to four.

teach.title: Find common denominator
teach.narration: Look at denominators two, four, six, and twelve; their least common multiple is twelve.

teach.title: Multiply both sides by 12
teach.narration: Multiply every term on both sides by positive twelve so all fractions disappear without flipping the inequality.

teach.title: Group constants and x terms
teach.narration: Add seven to both sides and subtract six x from both sides to put constants on the left and x terms on the right.

teach.title: Simplify both sides
teach.narration: Combine nine plus seven into sixteen and ten x minus six x into four x.

teach.title: Divide both sides by 4
teach.narration: Divide both sides by positive four to get four is less than or equal to x, which is x greater than or equal to four.

teach.title: Check boundary x = 4
teach.narration: Check at x equals four: both sides evaluate to eleven quarters, confirming four is the exact boundary.

teach.title: Final solution set
teach.narration: The solution of the inequality is x greater than or equal to four.

steps.title: Find common difference
steps.narration: From the fourth term to the tenth term is six equal steps totalling eighteen, so each step d is three.

steps.title: Divide by 6 steps
steps.narration: Divide eighteen by six on both sides to get common difference three.

steps.title: Step 20 terms past T_{4}
steps.narration: The twenty-fourth term is twenty steps ahead of the fourth term, so add twenty times three to thirteen.

steps.title: Twenty-fourth term
steps.narration: Thirteen plus sixty gives seventy-three.

teach.title: AP nth term formula
teach.narration: Recall the arithmetic progression formula T n equals first term a plus n minus one times common difference d.

teach.title: Write both given terms
teach.narration: Write equations for the tenth term with nine d and the fourth term with three d.

teach.title: Subtract to find d
teach.narration: Subtract the first equation from the second to eliminate a, leaving six d equals eighteen, so d equals three.

teach.title: Find first term a
teach.narration: Substitute d equals three into the fourth term equation and subtract nine from both sides to get a equals four.

teach.title: Compute 24th term
teach.narration: Put a equals four, n equals twenty-four, and d equals three into the nth term formula.

teach.title: Final term
teach.narration: Four plus sixty-nine equals seventy-three.

steps.title: Write common ratio
steps.narration: In a geometric progression, the common ratio equals the second term divided by the first term.

steps.title: Spot common factor \sqrt{2}
steps.narration: Notice that root two times root ten gives two root five, and root two times root five gives root ten.

steps.title: Factor out \sqrt{2} and cancel
steps.narration: Factor root two out of the numerator and cancel the shared bracket from top and bottom.

steps.title: Common ratio
steps.narration: Cancelling the matching factor leaves the common ratio as root two.

teach.title: State GP ratio formula
teach.narration: The common ratio of any geometric progression is the second term divided by the first term.

teach.title: Rewrite 2\sqrt{5} under one root
teach.narration: Bring two inside the square root as four to see two root five equals root twenty, which splits into root two times root ten.

teach.title: Split \sqrt{10}
teach.narration: Likewise, split root ten into root two times root five.

teach.title: Factor \sqrt{2} from T_{2}
teach.narration: Taking out the common factor root two reveals that the second term is simply root two times the first term.

teach.title: Divide and cancel T_{1}
teach.narration: Cancel the identical first-term expression from numerator and denominator.

teach.title: Final common ratio
teach.narration: Therefore the common ratio is root two.

steps.title: Expand matrix rows
steps.narration: Multiply each matrix row by column vector x, y to write two linear equations.

steps.title: Match x coefficients
steps.narration: Multiply the first equation by two and the second by five so both start with ten x.

steps.title: Subtract equations
steps.narration: Subtract the second scaled equation from the first to eliminate x and get twenty-three y equals sixty-nine.

steps.title: Value of y
steps.narration: Divide both sides by twenty-three to find y equals three.

teach.title: Set up matrix product
teach.narration: Write the mapping as multiplying the two by two matrix by the column vector x, y.

teach.title: Read two equations
teach.narration: Each row gives one linear equation: five x minus six y equals seven, and two x minus seven y equals minus eleven.

teach.title: Equalise x coefficients
teach.narration: Since we want y, multiply the first equation by two and the second by five so the x terms both become ten x.

teach.title: Subtract second from first
teach.narration: Subtract the second equation from the first carefully, watching the double minus signs on minus thirty-five y and minus fifty-five.

teach.title: Divide both sides by 23
teach.narration: Subtracting leaves twenty-three y equals sixty-nine; divide both sides by twenty-three to get y equals three.

teach.title: Verify in both rows
teach.narration: Putting y equals three into the first row gives x equals five, and two times five minus seven times three equals minus eleven.

teach.title: Final value of y
teach.narration: Therefore y equals three.

steps.title: Determinant formula
steps.narration: For a two by two matrix, subtract the off-diagonal product from the main diagonal product.

steps.title: Expand determinant
steps.narration: Multiply minus x by four and subtract twelve times minus one, setting it equal to minus twelve.

steps.title: Subtract 12 from both sides
steps.narration: Minus twelve times minus one becomes plus twelve; subtract twelve from both sides to get minus four x equals minus twenty-four.

steps.title: Value of x
steps.narration: Divide both sides by minus four to get x equals six.

teach.title: Compute determinant products
teach.narration: Multiply down the main diagonal minus x times four, then subtract the reverse diagonal twelve times minus one.

teach.title: Watch the double negative
teach.narration: Subtracting minus twelve adds twelve, so set minus four x plus twelve equal to minus twelve.

teach.title: Subtract 12 from both sides
teach.narration: Subtract twelve from both sides to get the x term on its own.

teach.title: Divide both sides by −4
teach.narration: Divide minus twenty-four by minus four; a negative divided by a negative gives positive six.

teach.title: Check determinant value
teach.narration: Check: replacing x with six gives minus twenty-four plus twelve, which equals minus twelve.

teach.title: Final value of x
teach.narration: Therefore x equals six.
